data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C nuclear energy company that has raised $125M+ to date. The broader nuclear sector comp universe includes 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms, with notable private peers including Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear sector—only 1 adjacent-stage peer was identified against a minimum threshold of 3 datapoints. Stage-progression methodology provides the sole applicable triangulation path, applying a standard 1.7x Series C-to-next-stage multiplier to the $125M raised proxy, yielding $212M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $181M to $244M, with a median implied value of $212M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer multiples for direct cross-check, reliance on a single methodological input, and the early-stage nature of nuclear technology companies, which typically exhibit wider valuation variance. Further refinement would require either narrowing the peer set to truly comparable development-stage and technology alignment or obtaining additional transaction comps from the nuclear sector.
